title: Setup 101
productJob: A compact durable reference for deciding whether information belongs in standing instructions, optional memory, one project or nowhere; not a provider walkthrough or class.
audience: A reader who wants an AI tool to stop starting from zero without putting the wrong information in the wrong place.
learnerOutcome: The reader can sort ordinary working context into four locations and identify when product, account or employer rules must be checked before saving anything.

mentalModel.standingInstructions: Stable preferences and recurring output rules that should apply broadly when the product supports them.
mentalModel.optionalMemory: A fact or preference the product may carry between conversations; it must be reviewable because it can become stale or wrong.
mentalModel.projectWorkspace: Files, instructions and context for one continuing job, subject to the product's actual account, plan, sharing and isolation behavior.
mentalModel.nowhere: Passwords, access tokens and material prohibited by law, agreement, employer policy or the governing account rules.
mentalModel.boundary: The sorting method can transfer between tools. The settings, data, availability and privacy behavior do not.

analogy.name: Three labelled places
analogy.mapping: Standing instructions are the note you reuse, memory is a pencil note that may need correcting, and a project is the labelled binder for one job.
analogy.limit: The labels explain the different jobs only. They do not prove that a product offers the feature, applies it everywhere, isolates the data or keeps it private.

items.reason: Potentially useful across chats, but likely to change and therefore reviewable.
Material for one continuing job, only if the governing account and policy allow it.
Specific to one job and likely to expire.
A secret credential does not belong in instructions, memory, a project or chat.
Use only after the contract, employer policy and approved account explicitly permit it.

sortingCheck.limitation: A placement answer is not upload authority. Product behavior and organizational rules remain decisive.
